finding.claim: GET /rss fetches an arbitrary attacker-supplied URL server-side and returns the first 400 bytes of the response to the caller, a non-blind full-response SSRF.
finding.source: params[:u], the `u` query parameter of GET /rss (app.rb:7-8), attacker-controlled and unauthenticated
finding.sink: URI.open(params[:u]).read at app.rb:8 (open-uri), with the response body echoed back at app.rb:9

trace.note: Sinatra route get "/rss" registered with no auth filter
params[:u] passed directly to URI.open, which makes an outbound HTTP(S)/FTP request to any host and port
open-uri follows HTTP redirects by default, so an allowed origin can redirect to an internal address
data[0, 400] returns the first 400 bytes of the fetched body to the attacker, making the SSRF readable rather than blind

finding.guards_checked: None. No scheme allowlist, no host or IP allowlist, no private/link-local/loopback block, no port restriction, no redirect limit or re-validation, no DNS-rebinding defense. data[0, 400] truncates output but does not validate input. require "open-uri" at app.rb:2 adds no protection.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only host check, TRUSTED.include?(uri.host) at app.rb:14, is in the /trusted route (app.rb:12-16) and does not cover /rss. The /rss handler at app.rb:7-9 has no allowlist, scheme, IP, or redirect check before URI.open(params[:u]) at app.rb:8.
verdict.reason: params[:u] at app.rb:8 flows unauthenticated from the GET /rss query string into URI.open with no validation, and the body is returned truncated to 400 bytes at app.rb:9, so the SSRF is readable. The trace lines match the code, and the open-uri redirect-following step is accurate library behavior.
